children: ) tagged a fresh intraday record high on Tuesday morning, extending a bull market that began in October 2022.

The milestone masks a sharp split inside the index. Among constituents valued at more than $20 billion, a handful remain so far below their own peaks that a full recovery would require gains of more than 200%.
The gap is widest at PG&E
. The utility firm, valued at about $27.2B, trades near $12.40, down 22.4% this year and 82.7% from its all-time high. Closing that distance would take a gain of roughly 480%. Moreover, PayPal
, at $46.5B and about $54 a share, sits 82.4% under its peak and would need a rise of about 470%.
are both below their respective all-time highs by roughly 81% and would require rallies of 437% and 427%, respectively.
The same pattern runs through consumer discretionary, health care, and real estate. Las Vegas Sands
would need a gain of about 306% to get back to record levels, while Zoetis
would need to close a gap of about 247%, and Crown Castle
would require a rise of about 211%.

Tuesday’s advance was led by technology and other megacap growth names as Treasury yields eased and oil slipped, with investors looking ahead to earnings. The record at the index level is real. Participation is not. For these large-cap holdouts, the distance back to prior highs is still measured in multiples, not in a routine catch-up rally.

title: S&P 500 hits a record; These $20B stocks still need 200% to break even
